significance: The largest Buddhist monument in the world: a stone mandala-mountain of nine terraces, 2,672 relief panels and 504 Buddhas, walking pilgrims from the world of desire through the world of forms to the formless summit stupa. Abandoned as Java turned to Islam, buried in ash, cleared under Raffles in 1814, and saved by the great UNESCO restoration of 1975–83; Vesak at Borobudur remains Indonesian Buddhism's central rite.
story: Javanese tradition names the divine architect Gunadharma, whose profile is traced in the Menoreh hills that watch the monument; the hidden 'Karmawibhangga' reliefs of cause and effect lie deliberately buried at the base — the law of karma literally underlying the whole mountain.
access: ~40 km from Yogyakarta; timed summit tickets via Borobudur Park.
